summary: Aa'isha reports that the Prophet never ate reclining and said he ate as a slave eats and sat as a slave sits.
notes: Addendum to an earlier narration; the report it adds to is not in this item. The cross-reference to Abdullaah bin Abbaas ('has already passed') is not tagged.

summary: Abu Ghaalib asked Abu Umaamah for a Hadith, and Abu Umaamah described the Prophet's dhikr, brief talks, long salaah and humility.
notes: Abu Ghaalib's Sahabi status is not stated in the text.

summary: Anas describes the Prophet's dhikr, plain clothing and riding, his acceptance of slaves' invitations, and his donkey at Khaybar.
The Prophet visited the sick and attended funerals.
notes: Opens with 'Another adds', a continuation of the previous Anas report. No narrator is named in this item; the heading names Anas, which is not used.

summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari says the Prophet rode a donkey, wore woollen clothes, milked a goat himself and served guests personally.

Ibn Abbaas says the Prophet sat and ate on the floor, milked a goat himself and accepted a slave's invitation to barley bread; another report adds that he accepted such an invitation in the middle of the night from a man of the upper part of Madinah.
notes: Two reports in one item: Ibn Abbaas's account, and the 'another narration' about the night invitation. The text reads 'Madman', which is read as Madinah.

summary: Anas says the Prophet accepted even plain food, and pawned his armour to a Jew, dying without the money to redeem it.
Umar says that each of the three times a man called the Prophet, he answered 'Labbaik'.
Abu Umaamah relates that a flirtatious woman mocked the Prophet for eating, was given food from his hand and mouth, and afterwards was overcome with modesty.
notes: The narrator reads 'Abu Umaamah Silg' in the OCR; taken as Abu Umaamah. The woman is unnamed.

summary: Jareer says the Prophet calmed a man who was trembling before him, telling him he was no king but the son of a Quraysh woman who ate dried meat.

Ibn Mas'ood reports the same calming of a trembling man on the day Makkah was conquered, and Aamir bin Rabee'ah says the Prophet took his shoe and would not let him fix its strap, disliking preferential treatment.
notes: Two reports: Ibn Mas'ood's and Aamir's. Aamir is the subject of his own account. The approved aamir-bin-rabeeah entry is marked unsure in the vocabulary.

summary: Abdullaah bin Jubayr says someone shaded the Prophet with a sheet, and he took it down, saying he was only a human being like them.
notes: Only one approved theme fits. Not in the approved people list.

summary: Abbaas wonders how long the Prophet will remain with them and asks why he has no raised platform; the Prophet says he prefers to stay among the people.
Ikramah reports Abbaas asking about the platform again, and concluding from the reply that the Prophet would be with them only a short while.
notes: The text marks Ikramah with (RA), but the vocabulary lists ikrimah as not a Companion. The id is used; please check. The Prophet's reply is 'the same as above', referring back to n01853.

summary: Aswad asks Aa'isha what the Prophet did on entering the house, and she says he did household chores and went to salaah when the time came.
notes: The text gives Aswad with no patronymic, so no approved id is assigned.

summary: Urwa and Amrah each ask Aa'isha what the Prophet did at home; she says he mended his shoes, stitched his clothes, removed lice from his clothing and milked his goat.
notes: Two reports: Urwa's and Amrah's. The text gives no patronymic for Urwa, so the approved urwa-bin-zubayr (unsure) is not assigned. An editorial footnote '(1) Bazzaar. Haythami...' is not part of the narration and is left out.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas says the Prophet never gave anyone the job of preparing his wudu or distributing his charity, and attended to both himself.
Jaabir says that when the Prophet came to visit him, he rode neither a mule nor a thoroughbred horse.
notes: Only one approved theme fits.

summary: Anas says the Prophet performed Hajj on an old carriage under a sheet worth about four Dirhams, and prayed for a Hajj free of show and boasting.
Anas says that when the Prophet entered Makkah at the conquest, he lowered his head onto his carriage out of humility.
notes: Two wordings of the same report from Anas, not two separate narrations.

summary: An unnamed narrator says that at Dhu Tuwa the Prophet stood on his carriage and lowered his head in gratitude to Allaah until his beard touched the middle of the carriage.
notes: Begins 'Another narration', so it is a separate report from the one before. The narrator is not named in this item.

summary: Abu Hurayrah says the Prophet bought trousers in the market and carried them himself, told the measurer to give the buyer the benefit, and pulled his hand away from a man who tried to kiss it.
notes: Two reports: Abu Hurayrah's account, and the 'another narration' that adds the measurer's words, followed by 'the rest is like the one above'. Abu Hurayrah is a participant in the story, so role is subject. The measurer and the man are unnamed.

summary: Aslam reports that when Umar rode a camel into Shaam, he rebuked people who looked at the mounts of unbelievers instead of those used by the Prophet and the Muslims.
Hishaam says he saw Umar stop a woman making aseedah and show her how to make it with a wooden spoon.
notes: Hishaam is not identified. It may be the Hishaam bin Khaalid of n01865, which is not confirmed by the text.

summary: Hishaam bin Khaalid says he heard Umar teach women to add flour only once the water is hot, stirring gradually to avoid lumps.
Zirr says he saw Umar walk barefoot to the Eid salaah.

Umar Makhzoomi reports Umar's sermon recalling how he herded for his Banu Makhzoom aunts for a few dates; Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf criticised it, and Umar said he had felt pride and wished to humble himself.
notes: Several versions of the sermon ('another narration'). The narrator is given as 'Umar Makhzoomi', which is not in the approved list and may not be Umar bin Khattaab, so please check. Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf speaks in the story and is tagged subject.

summary: Hasan says that Umar, walking out on a hot day, asked a boy on a donkey for a ride and then rode behind him into Madinah.
notes: Hasan is not identified. The approved list has Hasan bin Ali and Hasan bin Abil Hasan (no), so no id is assigned. Ends with an OCR marker '(1 *'. Only one approved theme fits.

summary: A boy recounts that Umar, with a lash, sent other boys scattering from the fallen dates, did not hit him when he saw the dates in his garment, and walked him home.
notes: The narrator's name is missing from the text ('Hadhrat (RA) says') and is not tagged.

summary: Maalik's grandfather says he saw Umar and Uthmaan each carry a youngster on the ride into Madinah; the narrator explains this as humility and benefit to others, and criticises rulers who make youths walk behind them.
notes: The reporter is the unnamed grandfather of Hadhrat Maalik; Maalik is named only as the link. Maalik is not matched to any approved id.

summary: Maymoon bin Mahraan says he saw Uthmaan, while Khalifah, ride a mule with his slave Naa'il riding behind him.
notes: Maymoon reports from an unnamed man of Hamdaan, who is not tagged.

summary: Abdullaah Roomi says Uthmaan drew his own water for night wudu and never woke his household for Tahajjud; the grandmother of Zubayr bin Abdullaah, once his servant, adds that he fasted constantly.
notes: Two reports: Abdullaah Roomi's, and the grandmother's, which comes through Zubayr bin Abdullaah. The grandmother is unnamed and not tagged. Zubayr bin Abdullaah is not matched to the approved Zubayr entries.

summary: Hasan says he saw Uthmaan sleeping in the Masjid under a shawl with no one around him, though he was then Ameerul Mu'mineen.
notes: Hasan is not identified (see n01868).

summary: Unaysa says Abu Bakr milked goats for the girls of the locality, and kept doing so after he became Khalifah, asking them how they wanted the milk.
notes: The author cross-references narrations from Aa'isha, Abdullaah bin Umar and Ibn Musayyab in an earlier chapter; those are not tagged. Ibn Afraa, named in Abu Bakr's words, is not tagged.

summary: Saalih, a blanket merchant, reports that his grandfather saw Ali buy dates for a Dirham and refuse help to carry them.
notes: Saalih is not identified (the approved list has several Saalihs). The grandfather is the eyewitness and is unnamed. Only one approved theme fits.

summary: Zaadhaan reports that Ali walked the market guiding lost people, announcing lost items and helping the weak, and recited a verse about the Hereafter, saying it was revealed about just and humble rulers.
notes: The verse (Qasas 28:83) is quoted in the text.

summary: Jurmooz saw Ali leave his house in two reddish cloths, walk the market with a lash, and urge traders to fear Allaah, deal amiably and give full weight and measure.

Abu Matar recounts Ali's episodes in the market: he warned against oaths in trade, made a date seller take back dates sold to a servant, banned dead fish, and refused a refund a cloth merchant's father tried to give him.
notes: One narrator recounts several episodes; kept as one narration. Abu Matar is a participant (he identifies Ali to the trader), so role is subject. The other traders are unnamed.

summary: Ataa reports that Faatima's plaits hit the bowl as she kneaded dough, and Mutallib bin Abdullaah says Ummu Salamah, who had married the Prophet that evening, was grinding flour later that night.
notes: Two reports: Ataa's on Faatima, and Mutallib bin Abdullaah's on Ummu Salamah. The Prophet is mentioned as the husband of Ummu Salamah and the father of Faatima.

summary: Salaamah Ajali says he and his cousin Qudaamah went to see Salmaan Faarsi, and found him weaving palm baskets while in command of twenty thousand men; Salmaan prayed that Allaah love the cousin.
notes: The text's quotation of Salmaan's reply is cut ('saying:' followed by no words), an OCR gap.
